page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, with no simultaneous multithreading. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a bundled 2850 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in data decompression and compression, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression reaching 635.79 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression at 36.5 GB/sec. Database operations and memory performance are also highly rated, as evidenced by a PassMark database operations score of 46541.54 and Redis SET operations reaching 136.39 million operations per second. However, while prompt processing for small language models is exceptionally fast at 4218.03 tokens/sec, text generation speeds for the same small model fall into the lower tier at 31.56 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m9gd.12xlarge offers a high-density resource profile by combining dedicated ARMv9 cores, a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, and high-capacity local NVMe storage. This combination eliminates the need for separate network-attached storage fees for high-I/O workloads. The instance is highly suited for database hosting, high-throughput web serving, Redis caching layers, and data compression pipelines. It is less optimal for workloads requiring specialized x86 instruction sets or high-performance GPU acceleration.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose, ARM64-based server instance powered by a 48-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor running at 3.3 GHz. It features 192.0 GB of RAM, a 2850 GB local NVMe SSD, and 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance delivers top-tier performance in database operations, Redis caching, and data compression, as demonstrated by 136.39 million Redis SET operations per second and 635.79 GB/sec multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. While prompt processing for small language models is highly efficient, text generation speeds are relatively low. The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is high for workloads requiring local, high-speed NVMe storage alongside balanced compute resources. It is best suited for database hosting, high-throughput web serving, and caching workloads.
